title: First look at TEF and TCF
goal: Understand how TEF Canada and TCF Canada work, try a few exam-style tasks at your level, and start thinking about which exam suits you.

example.fr: L'épreuve d'expression orale dure quinze minutes.
example.en: The speaking section lasts fifteen minutes.

items.note: False friend: passer un examen = to take it; réussir un examen = to pass it.

example.fr: J'ai besoin du niveau 7 dans les quatre compétences.
example.en: I need level 7 in all four skills.

example.fr: Les résultats sont valides deux ans.
example.en: The results are valid for two years.

blocks.title: Two exams, one Canadian scale
blocks.body:
If you want to prove your French to the Government of Canada (IRCC), the two French tests you will hear about are **TEF Canada** and **TCF Canada**.

- **TEF Canada** (*Test d'évaluation de français*) is run by **Le français des affaires**, part of the Paris Île-de-France Chamber of Commerce (CCI Paris Île-de-France).
- **TCF Canada** (*Test de connaissance du français*) is run by **France Éducation international**.

Both test the **four skills**: reading, listening, writing and speaking. Your score in **each skill** is converted to a Canadian level called **NCLC** (*Niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens*, the French equivalent of CLB). Programs then ask for a minimum NCLC in each skill.

Today you'll see how each exam is built, try a few tasks **at A2 level**, and get some first advice on choosing. You don't need to be ready for an exam yet: this is a first look.

Rules, accepted tests, fees and minimum levels **change**. For any real decision, check the official IRCC website and the exam provider's website. IRCC generally requires language test results that are **less than two years old** when you apply.

blocks.title: TEF Canada
head: Skill
Time
What you do
rows: 40 multiple-choice questions on documents; 1 point each, no penalty for a wrong answer
40 multiple-choice questions on recordings, usually heard once
A: continue a news article, 80–120 words (about 25 min). B: give and justify your point of view, 200–250 words (about 35 min)
A: get information about a document (an ad, a flyer) by asking questions, with vous (5 min). B: convince a friend to do something, with tu (10 min)
blocks.note: All four tests must be taken **on the same day** for the certificate to be recognized. Results show a score out of 699 and an *équivalence ancien score*; IRCC uses the *équivalence ancien score* for each skill. Results are valid for **2 years**.

blocks.title: TCF Canada
head: Skill
Time
What you do
rows: 39 multiple-choice questions; recordings get harder as you go
39 multiple-choice questions; documents get harder as you go

Task 1: a message, 60–120 words (about 15 min). Task 2: an article, letter or report on an experience, 120–150 words (about 20 min). Task 3: present two opposing views, then take a position, 120–180 words (about 25 min)
Task 1: guided interview about yourself, no preparation. Task 2: ask the examiner questions to get information (2 min preparation). Task 3: give and justify your opinion on a topic
blocks.note: Total duration is about **2 h 47**. Listening and reading are scored from **0 to 699**; writing and speaking from **0 to 20**. The exact timing of each speaking task is commonly reported as about 2, 5½ and 4½ minutes: check the official candidate handbook.

blocks.title: Side by side
head: TEF Canada
TCF Canada
rows: Le français des affaires (CCI Paris Île-de-France)
2 tasks: news article (80–120 words) + opinion (200–250 words)
3 tasks: message (60–120) + article (120–150) + two views and your opinion (120–180)
2 tasks, 15 min: get information (vous), convince a friend (tu)
3 tasks, about 12 min: interview, interaction, opinion
Out of 699 per skill, with an équivalence ancien score used by IRCC
0–699 for listening and reading, 0–20 for writing and speaking
blocks.note: Both are accepted by IRCC and measure the same thing in the end: your **NCLC level in each of the four skills**.

blocks.title: What NCLC level do you need?
blocks.body:
Each skill gets **its own** NCLC level; they are not averaged. A program that asks for NCLC 7 usually needs NCLC 7 in **each** required skill, so one weak skill can block you.

- **Canadian citizenship:** applicants aged 18 to 54 currently need **CLB / NCLC 4** in **speaking and listening**, in English **or** French.
- **Express Entry, Federal Skilled Worker program:** you currently need at least **CLB / NCLC 7 in all four abilities in your *first* official language**. That language can be English or French, so French NCLC 7 is **not** required of everyone.
- **French as a bonus:** strong French results earn **extra Express Entry points**, even when French is your second official language, and IRCC holds **draws for French-speaking candidates**.

These rules change often: **check IRCC** for the current requirements before you decide anything.

NCLC and the CEFR levels of this course (A1, A2, B1, B2) are different scales and do not match exactly. As a rough guide, **NCLC 7 typically needs solid B1–B2 skills**: well beyond A2. That's why the B1 and B2 levels of FrenchQuest are built around exam tasks.

blocks.title: Choosing between TEF and TCF
blocks.body:
Neither exam is “easier”: they measure the same levels. Choose based on **format, practicality and your strengths**:

- **Writing:** TEF asks for one long text (200–250 words) and a news-style continuation. TCF has three shorter tasks, starting with a 60–120 word message, the kind of text you wrote in unit 11.
- **Speaking:** TEF is two role-plays (a phone call with vous, then convincing a friend with tu). TCF starts with an interview about you, then an interaction and an opinion.
- **Reading and listening:** both are multiple choice. TCF questions get harder through the test, so bank the easy points early.
- **Practical things:** test centres near you, available dates, fees and how fast you need results. These vary by city.
- **Try both:** do a sample task of each in the **Exam Lab**, then choose the format where you feel most comfortable.

blocks.title: Common myths and traps
blocks.body:
- **“I passed the exam” = [[J'ai réussi l'examen]].** [[J'ai passé l'examen]] only means you took it.
- **Leaving blanks:** in TEF reading there is no penalty for a wrong answer, so a blank scores the same as a wrong answer: answer every question.
- **Ignoring word counts:** too short or too long costs points in both exams.
- **Preparing only grammar:** exams reward completing the **task**: answering every part, the right register (tu or vous), and clear organization.
- **Taking the exam too early:** you pay for each attempt. Use mock tasks to check you're close to your target level first.

TEF Canada and TCF Canada are the versions designed for IRCC. Québec's own immigration programs also accept French tests (including versions of these exams), with their own rules: if you plan to settle in Québec, check the Québec government's immigration website as well. For citizenship, French or English is accepted; you only need one official language.

steps.title: Exam-style sample items (A2 level)
steps.intro: These are original practice items written in the style of the exams, at A2 level. Real exam items start around this level and become much harder. Play each recording **only once**, as in the real test.

blocks.title: Document A
blocks.fr:
PISCINE MUNICIPALE DU PARC LAFONTAINE
À cause de travaux, la piscine sera fermée du 3 au 16 juillet.
Pendant cette période, les membres peuvent utiliser gratuitement la piscine du centre Jean-Claude-Malépart, avec leur carte habituelle.

blocks.prompt: What does this notice tell members?
options: They can swim at another pool for free during the closure
They must buy a new card for July
The pool will close earlier in the evenings in July
blocks.explain: [[Les membres peuvent utiliser gratuitement la piscine du centre…]]: the right option **rephrases** the text (*another pool for free*), as in the real exams. Their usual card works ([[avec leur carte habituelle]]).

blocks.title: Document B
blocks.fr:
Objet : Notre souper de jeudi

Bonjour Mei,
Je suis vraiment désolée, mais je ne pourrai pas venir jeudi : mon patron m'a demandé de remplacer une collègue malade. Est-ce qu'on pourrait se voir la semaine prochaine ? Mardi ou mercredi, je suis libre. C'est moi qui t'invite, cette fois !
Anne

blocks.prompt: Why is Anne writing to Mei?
options: To cancel their supper and suggest another day
To invite Mei to her workplace
To ask Mei to replace a sick colleague
blocks.explain: Exam questions often ask about the **purpose** of a document. Anne cancels ([[je ne pourrai pas venir jeudi]]) and suggests next week ([[Est-ce qu'on pourrait se voir la semaine prochaine ?]]). She's the one replacing a colleague, not Mei.

blocks.fr: Bonjour, c'est Martine, de l'agence Bel Appart. Je vous appelle au sujet de votre visite de demain. Le propriétaire ne sera pas là le matin, alors je vous propose de venir à 15 h au lieu de 10 h. Si ça ne vous convient pas, rappelez-moi avant ce soir.
blocks.en: Hello, it's Martine from the Bel Appart agency. I'm calling about your viewing tomorrow. The owner won't be there in the morning, so I suggest you come at 3 p.m. instead of 10 a.m. If that doesn't suit you, call me back before tonight.
options: To change the time of tomorrow's viewing
To cancel the viewing
To move the viewing to another day
blocks.explain: [[À 15 h au lieu de 10 h]]: same day ([[demain]]), new time. You only call back if it **doesn't** work for you.

blocks.fr: Mesdames et messieurs, nous arrivons bientôt à Ottawa. Les passagers qui continuent vers Toronto doivent changer de train. Le train pour Toronto partira de la voie 3 dans vingt-cinq minutes.
blocks.en: Ladies and gentlemen, we will soon arrive in Ottawa. Passengers continuing to Toronto must change trains. The train to Toronto will leave from track 3 in twenty-five minutes.
blocks.prompt: You are going to Toronto. What must you do?
options: Get off in Ottawa and take another train from track 3
Stay on this train until Toronto
Wait twenty-five minutes on this train
blocks.explain: [[Les passagers qui continuent vers Toronto doivent changer de train]]: change trains in Ottawa. The new train leaves [[de la voie 3 dans vingt-cinq minutes]].

blocks.fr: Allô, Karim ? C'est Sofia. Écoute, je suis vraiment désolée pour hier soir. J'ai complètement oublié notre rendez-vous au restaurant ! J'ai travaillé très tard et je n'ai pas regardé mon téléphone. Je peux t'inviter samedi pour me faire pardonner ?
blocks.en: Hello, Karim? It's Sofia. Listen, I'm really sorry about last night. I completely forgot our restaurant date! I worked very late and I didn't look at my phone. Can I invite you on Saturday to make it up to you?
blocks.prompt: What is the main purpose of Sofia's call?
options: To apologize and offer to make it up to him
To complain that Karim was late
To book a table at a restaurant
blocks.explain: Listening tests often ask about the speaker's **intention**. [[Je suis vraiment désolée]] (apology) + [[Je peux t'inviter samedi]] (an offer): she apologizes and invites him. [[Pour me faire pardonner]] = to make it up to you.

blocks.title: Document C
blocks.fr: Recherchons animateur ou animatrice pour le camp de jour de la Ville de Gatineau, du 30 juin au 15 août. Vous avez 18 ans ou plus, vous aimez les enfants et vous parlez français ? Une formation de deux jours est offerte en juin. Expérience non nécessaire. 18 $ de l'heure.

blocks.prompt: Who can apply for this job?
options: An adult who speaks French and likes children, even without experience
Only people with experience in a day camp
Teenagers under 18 who speak French
blocks.explain: [[18 ans ou plus]], [[vous aimez les enfants]], [[vous parlez français]], and [[expérience non nécessaire]] (experience not needed).

steps.title: Check your understanding of the exams
steps.intro: Seven quick questions about what you've just learned.

blocks.prompt: TEF Canada reading: how long is it, and how many questions are there?
options: 60 minutes, 40 questions
40 minutes, 40 questions
60 minutes, 39 questions
blocks.explain: TEF reading: 60 min, 40 questions. 40 min is TEF listening; 39 questions is TCF reading and listening.

blocks.prompt: How many writing tasks are there in TCF Canada?
options: Three
Two
One long essay
blocks.explain: TCF: a message (60–120 words), an article or report (120–150) and a text comparing two views with your opinion (120–180). TEF has two tasks.

blocks.prompt: In TEF Canada speaking, section A, what do you do?
options: Ask questions to get information about a document, using vous
Convince a friend to do something, using tu
Talk about yourself without preparation
blocks.explain: Section A: *obtenir des renseignements*, around ten polite questions with vous. Section B is convincing a friend. The interview about yourself is TCF task 1.

blocks.prompt: How are TCF Canada writing and speaking scored?
options: From 0 to 20
From 0 to 699
From NCLC 1 to NCLC 12 directly
blocks.explain: TCF writing and speaking: 0–20. Listening and reading: 0–699. Each score is then converted to an NCLC level.

blocks.prompt: Which statement about NCLC is correct?
options: Each skill gets its own NCLC level
NCLC is the average of the four skills
NCLC 7 is the same as A2
blocks.explain: Each skill is converted separately, and programs set minimums per skill. NCLC 7 typically needs solid B1–B2 skills, well above A2.
[[Réussir]] = to pass. [[J'ai passé l'examen]] only means *I took the exam*.

blocks.prompt: Match each task with its exam.
pairs: Present two views, then your opinion

steps.title: Try two exam-style tasks
steps.intro: Do these under exam conditions: set a timer, no dictionary, no translator. At A2, the goal is to **complete every part of the task**, not to sound perfect.

blocks.prompt: TCF-style writing task 1 (15 minutes, 60–120 words). A French-speaking friend is coming to visit your city for the first time next month. Write a message to tell them what the city is like, what you'll do together, and what they should bring.
blocks.promptFr: Un ami va visiter votre ville pour la première fois le mois prochain. Écrivez-lui un message : décrivez la ville, dites ce que vous allez faire ensemble et ce qu'il doit apporter. (60 à 120 mots)
checklist: Every part of the task: the city, the activities, what to bring
Register: tu, an informal greeting and closing
Future: futur simple or aller + infinitive
Advice: tu devrais / il faut + infinitive
Comparisons or descriptions: plus… que, c'est…, il y a…
Between 60 and 120 words; reread for agreement and accents

models.label: A2 model
models.fr:
Salut Thomas !
Je suis très content de ta visite le mois prochain ! Ottawa est une petite ville, mais elle est très jolie, avec beaucoup de parcs et de musées. Samedi, nous visiterons le Parlement et le marché By. Le soir, on mangera dans un bon restaurant libanais. Dimanche, on ira à Gatineau à vélo. En octobre, il fait déjà froid ici, alors tu devrais apporter un manteau chaud et de bonnes chaussures.
À bientôt !
Raj
models.en: Hi Thomas! I'm very happy about your visit next month! Ottawa is a small city, but it's very pretty, with lots of parks and museums. On Saturday, we'll visit Parliament and the ByWard Market. In the evening, we'll eat in a good Lebanese restaurant. On Sunday, we'll go to Gatineau by bike. In October it's already cold here, so you should bring a warm coat and good shoes. See you soon! Raj

models.label: Strong A2 model
models.fr:
Coucou Inès !
J'ai trop hâte de te voir ! Tu vas adorer Montréal : c'est une ville plus grande que Lyon, très vivante, et on y parle français et anglais. Le premier jour, on se promènera dans le Vieux-Montréal, puis on montera au mont Royal pour voir la ville d'en haut. Samedi, je t'emmènerai au marché Jean-Talon, et le soir, on ira voir un spectacle dans un petit bar. Attention : en novembre, il peut faire zéro degré, et parfois il neige déjà ! Il faut apporter une tuque, des gants et des bottes imperméables.
Bises,
Sofia
models.en: Hey Inès! I can't wait to see you! You're going to love Montréal: it's a bigger city than Lyon, very lively, and people speak French and English there. On the first day, we'll walk around Old Montréal, then we'll go up Mount Royal to see the city from above. On Saturday, I'll take you to the Jean-Talon market, and in the evening we'll go to see a show in a little bar. Careful: in November it can be zero degrees, and sometimes it's already snowing! You need to bring a toque (tuque, the Québec word for a winter hat), gloves and waterproof boots. Hugs, Sofia

blocks.title: Document for the speaking task
blocks.fr:
ÉCHANGE LINGUISTIQUE
Vous voulez pratiquer votre français ? Rencontrez un francophone qui veut apprendre votre langue !
Rencontres au café de la bibliothèque centrale.
Inscription : Mme Leblanc, 613 555-0182
blocks.en: LANGUAGE EXCHANGE. Do you want to practise your French? Meet a French speaker who wants to learn your language! Meetings at the central library café. Registration: Ms. Leblanc, 613-555-0182

blocks.prompt: TEF-style speaking, section A (about 2 minutes). You call Madame Leblanc about the language exchange above. Introduce yourself and ask as many different questions as you can (at least eight): days and times, how it works, cost, level, who you meet, how long, how to register… Use vous and imagine her answers.
blocks.promptFr: Vous téléphonez à Madame Leblanc pour avoir des renseignements sur l'échange linguistique.
checklist: Greeting and reason for the call: Je vous appelle au sujet de…
At least eight different questions, with varied question words
Two or three indirect questions: J'aimerais savoir si… / Je voudrais savoir combien…
Vous throughout; polite reactions: D'accord, très bien, ah bon ?
A natural closing: Merci beaucoup pour ces renseignements, bonne journée !

models.label: A2 model
models.fr: Bonjour, madame Leblanc. Je m'appelle Mei Chen. Je vous appelle au sujet de l'échange linguistique. Quand est-ce que les rencontres ont lieu ? … Le mardi soir, d'accord. À quelle heure ? … Et ça dure combien de temps ? … Est-ce que c'est gratuit ? … Très bien. Je parle chinois et anglais : est-ce que je peux trouver un partenaire ? … Je voudrais savoir si mon niveau est assez bon. J'ai le niveau A2. … Ah, parfait ! Comment est-ce que je peux m'inscrire ? … Est-ce que je dois apporter quelque chose ? … Merci beaucoup pour ces renseignements. Bonne journée !
models.en: Hello, Ms. Leblanc. My name is Mei Chen. I'm calling about the language exchange. When do the meetings take place? … Tuesday evenings, OK. At what time? … And how long does it last? … Is it free? … Very good. I speak Chinese and English: can I find a partner? … I'd like to know if my level is good enough. I'm at A2 level. … Oh, perfect! How can I register? … Do I need to bring anything? … Thank you very much for this information. Have a good day! (The … mark the answers you imagine.)

models.label: Strong A2 model
models.fr: Bonjour, madame ! Ici Karim Haddad. J'ai vu votre affiche à la bibliothèque, et l'échange linguistique m'intéresse beaucoup. J'aimerais d'abord savoir comment ça fonctionne : on parle français tout le temps, ou une partie en français et une partie dans l'autre langue ? … Ah, moitié-moitié, c'est une bonne idée. Je parle arabe : est-ce qu'il y a des francophones qui veulent apprendre l'arabe ? … Super. Les rencontres ont lieu quel jour, et à quelle heure ? … Le jeudi, c'est parfait, parce que je travaille le mardi soir. Est-ce qu'il faut payer quelque chose ? … Seulement le café, d'accord ! Je voudrais aussi savoir si on rencontre toujours la même personne. … Et la première rencontre, c'est quand ? … Comment est-ce que je m'inscris, par téléphone ou par courriel ? … Très bien. Je vous remercie beaucoup, madame, et bonne fin de journée !
models.en: Hello, madam! This is Karim Haddad. I saw your poster at the library, and I'm very interested in the language exchange. First, I'd like to know how it works: do we speak French all the time, or part in French and part in the other language? … Oh, half and half, that's a good idea. I speak Arabic: are there French speakers who want to learn Arabic? … Great. What day and what time are the meetings? … Thursdays, that's perfect, because I work on Tuesday evenings. Do you have to pay anything? … Only for the coffee, OK! I'd also like to know if you always meet the same person. … And when is the first meeting? … How do I register, by phone or by email? … Very good. Thank you very much, madam, and have a good evening! (The … mark the answers you imagine.)

blocks.title: Exam-style challenge: TEF speaking, section B
blocks.body:
Ready for a taste of B1? Use the same document. This time, a **friend** doesn't want to join the language exchange: [[Je suis trop timide, et je n'ai pas le temps.]] Convince them in **one minute**, with **tu**: give at least three reasons, answer both objections, and stay friendly.

Useful starters: [[Tu sais, …]] [[En plus, …]] [[Je te comprends, mais…]] [[Tu verras, …]] [[Allez, viens avec moi !]]

In the real TEF, this section lasts about ten minutes and the examiner keeps objecting: arguing for that long is a B1–B2 skill, and it's exactly what the next levels of this course will train.

steps.title: A2 is complete: what comes next

blocks.title: What A2 means
blocks.body:
**Bravo !** Finishing A2 means you can **manage familiar situations on your own**. You can now:

- talk about the past with the **passé composé** and the **imparfait**, and tell a short story from your life
- talk about plans with the **futur proche** and the **futur simple**
- buy tickets, book a hotel, explain a health problem, deal with a landlord, compare and return items, organize an outing
- use pronouns like [[le, lui, leur, y, en]] to sound more natural
- write practical messages in the right register: a text to a friend, a request, a complaint, a reply to an ad

blocks.title: Your next steps
blocks.body:
- **The Exam Lab is now recommended.** Open it to see each exam's format in detail, try timed tasks, and get an honest estimate of where you stand. Don't worry about low estimates at this stage: they show you the road ahead.
- **Set a realistic target.** If you need **NCLC 7 in French** (for example, if French is your first official language for Express Entry, or to get the French bonus points), plan for **solid B1–B2 skills** in all four abilities. Check IRCC for the exact level your program needs. That usually takes many more months of regular practice after A2.
- **Keep going with B1.** You'll learn to give and defend opinions, tell complete stories, write connected paragraphs and speak at length: exactly what TEF and TCF ask for. B1 also includes a full unit of exam strategies.
- **Practise a little every day:** 15 minutes of reviews, plus some real French: the radio, a podcast, a conversation group, a language exchange.

summary:
- **Bravo ! You have finished A2.** You can manage everyday situations, talk about the past and the future, and write practical messages
- You know how **TEF Canada** and **TCF Canada** are built (four skills, timings, task types, scores) and that results are converted to an **NCLC level for each skill**
- **NCLC 7 typically needs solid B1–B2 skills**: open the **Exam Lab** to practise exam tasks, and continue with **B1**
